error: npm ERR! ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
meaning: npm refused to install because two packages need incompatible versions of the same peer dependency, usually React. Since npm 7, peer conflicts stop the install instead of just warning.
causes: The AI added a library that only supports an older React (e.g. requires react@^17 or ^18) while the project uses React 19.
Mixed major versions of a framework family (e.g. @tanstack, eslint plugins, date-fns adapters).
The lockfile was deleted or regenerated with a different npm version on the build server.

steps.text: Read the lines after 'Could not resolve dependency': they name the package and the peer it wants, for example 'peer react@"^18" from some-lib'.
Best fix: upgrade the offending package to a version that supports your React.
steps.code:
npm view some-lib peerDependencies
npm install some-lib@latest

steps.text: If none exists, pin React to the version the library supports, or swap the library for a maintained alternative.
Temporary workaround (still deploys): tell npm to use old peer behaviour, locally and on the host.
Commit package-lock.json so Vercel/Netlify install the exact same tree.

prompt: npm install fails with ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree. Here is the full error: <PASTE>. Identify which package has the conflicting peer dependency, upgrade it to a version compatible with our React version (or suggest a maintained replacement), and only if no compatible version exists add legacy-peer-deps=true to .npmrc. Do not use --force.

faq.a: Usually works, but you may run a library on a React version it was not tested with. Prefer upgrading.

faq.q: Why does it build locally but not on Vercel?
faq.a: Your local node_modules may be old; the host installs fresh from package.json and the lockfile.
